claims.text: Factory Missions uses an orchestrator, a fresh worker session for each feature, and fresh validators injected at milestones; validators surface issues but do not fix them.

Factory's Missions orchestrator writes validation-contract.md, containing behavioral assertions such as VAL-AUTH-001, before features are implemented so that validation is not shaped by the implementation.
Factory's Slack-clone mission took 16.5 hours, with validation accounting for 37.2% of the time.
Factory's Slack-clone mission used 185 agent runs and 778.5M tokens, of which 744.9M were cache reads.
In Factory's Slack-clone mission, milestones passing per validation round went 0/6, 1/6, 2/6, then 6/6.
In Factory's Slack-clone mission, fix features made up 34.4% of implementation work (21 of 61 features).
Factory reports that 14% of Missions run longer than 24 hours.
Factory says the Missions orchestrator still sometimes scopes work too broadly.
Factory 2.0, dated June 15 2026, claims model independence via a router, sovereign deployment options, and continual learning, without providing benchmarks or implementation detail.
